cells.tense: You are here, holding what you have learned together without needing it kept.
cells.ask: Say plainly out loud to one person what you have come to understand about how this works — no argument, once through — and let that be enough.
cells.core:
You can look at something concrete and see the shape underneath it, and the shape doesn't lie to you. What you understand this way comes out useful — to you, and to whoever is near enough to hear it. There's no forcing in it. Things have finished becoming what they are, and you can let them be that.

That's why people bring you their situations. You don't hand back slogans; you hand back the mechanism, stripped and whole. It's the same clarity you keep for yourself. This isn't a trick you perform — it's the natural end of paying attention for a long time, which is what makes it quiet rather than clever.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what holds a thing together and say it plain.
cells.verb: stripping the concrete away to see the mechanism underneath
cells.place: the place where things come together and let go

cells.tense: You are standing past the end of this, treating a next thing as already decided.
cells.ask: Pick one tangle you keep re-reading and put its pieces on paper in front of you — what's actually here, one line each — then close the notebook.
cells.core:
You're reading patterns that aren't there yet. Something doesn't add up in one place, so your mind runs it again, then again, and each pass turns up a further layer — until you're reasoning about why someone glanced the way they did, and the reasoning has no floor. You're not enjoying this. You're just ahead of it, trying to close a loop that isn't looping.

The part that's hard to say: the analysis used to be the pleasure, and now it runs without you. Your mind keeps handing you structures that explain everything and finish nothing. That's not clarity. It's your gift running on no raw material, chewing itself.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern-sense won't stop, and it's inventing patterns now.

cells.tense: You are taking things at face value and you are still there.
cells.ask: Take one story you know — told to you by someone older, or one you tell — and notice what it is actually doing when it is retold, then say that part once.
cells.core:
Taken at face value, a story is only its events. But you've sat with enough of them to notice how they carry a lesson, a warning, a way of doing things — and when that reading is working, you can pass the meaning on without preaching it. You can hear what a room is doing under what it says, and let it stay simple until it's useful to say more.

Lately you've kept to the plain facts and the literal words. It keeps loose meanings out and it shuts the deeper reading down — so what you noticed over the years stays where it was made and doesn't travel. Nothing has to be believed for that to open again; just read the story for what it's doing.
cells.sheetLine: You read things at face value and the meaning stays put.

cells.tense: You are already arranging this, and describing the arrangement as luck or other people's doing.
cells.ask: Name one recurring place you keep ending up — the kind of job, or the kind of person — and say out loud what it is that keeps putting you there.
cells.core:
There's a shape to what keeps happening around you. People show up in a certain order, the same kind of request arrives, and you call it coincidence or just how the world works. Some of the arranging is yours — you decide who hears what, which door you walk through — and you don't count it as yours.

Nobody is asking you to take the blame for the pattern; only to see that you have a hand in it. When you can name the shape as something you participate in, then it's not something that simply happens to you — it's something you can do differently. That part hasn't been said yet.
cells.sheetLine: You're arranging this and calling it coincidence.
